title: TypeScript SDK: Consumer-snapshot handshake for resumable AsyncIterator <-> WebStream interop
creator: Arielle Chen
description: Introduce a light-weight consumer snapshot + handshake primitive in the TypeScript SDK that enables graceful consumer takeover and resumable consumption across AsyncIterator and Web Stream surfaces. The goal is to provide a deterministic, minimal snapshot token that external consumers (e.g., apps, server functions, browser clients) can persist and later use to resume a partially-consumed streaming response without losing tokens or duplicating output. This ticket scopes the API shape, runtime invariants, tests, docs, and an example migration for streaming-based features that need resume or consumer-switching semantics.
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes a StreamSnapshot type (opaque string token) and APIs: .snapshot(), fromSnapshot(token) and .toWebStream()/fromAsyncIterator() helpers
Resuming from a snapshot continues the stream from the byte/token position recorded in the snapshot with no duplicated application-visible chunks (idempotent resume).
Interop conversion preserves backpressure semantics in Node/browser: AsyncIterator consumer can pause/resume, WebStream consumer sees correct highWaterMark behavior.
Comprehensive unit tests that fuzz partial-consumption, abrupt consumer swap, and retry-on-network-failure scenarios.
End-to-end integration example in examples/ts/resumable-handshake demonstrating browser-to-server resume flow.
Docs and migration guide published in SDK changelog and examples folder before release cut.
Performance regression <5% for common streaming workloads (validated by CI microbenchmarks).
discussion: 2026-03-10 Arielle: Initial spike showed snapshot token can be a base64-encoded JSON containing sequence cursor + checksum + stream schema version.
2026-03-10 Diego: Concern about exposing internal offsets—we'll keep token opaque and validate checksum server-side to avoid coupling.
2026-03-11 Priya Nair (Review): Prefer not to expand SDK surface with many helper variants. Keep high-level helpers only and document low-level interop recipe.
2026-03-11 Implementation decision: snapshot API will not expose exact byte offsets; server accepts snapshot tokens and validates; server-side compatibility window will be 6 months for tokens.
2026-03-12 Diego: Demo branch created with basic snapshot serialization and AsyncIterator resume harness. Draft PR opened for review.
implementation_notes: Add StreamSnapshot = string alias in SDK; server accepts snapshot token via resume_from query param or Authorization-like header.

Implement Stream.snapshot(): Promise<string> that produces base64(JSON) token with {cursor, version, hmac} where hmac signs cursor+version using server key. SDK will use server-provided token string; no local signing.
Provide helpers: Stream.fromAsyncIterator(iterable) -> Stream, stream.toWebStream() -> ReadableStream, and Stream.fromSnapshot(token) -> Stream resume factory.

Edge cases: if backend reports 'snapshot expired' error, SDK should surface a specific Status code and a Retry-After header in the error object for callers to decide fallback (e.g., restart from scratch).
Node vs Browser: use built-in ReadableStream in browsers; Node runtime uses web-streams-polyfill when running integration tests in CI (already present).

Backpressure mapping: AsyncIterator.next() will await underlying pull if queue full; converting to WebStream must honor controller.enqueue() only when desired size allows; implement a small adaptive buffer to smooth differences.
Telemetry: emit metric 'snapshot.created' and 'snapshot.resumed' with tags for success/failure and latency to resume.
test_plan: Unit tests: serialize/deserialize snapshot token, token tampering -> rejection, expired token -> specific error code.
Property fuzz: partially consume 0..N chunks then snapshot, persist token, create new consumer from snapshot and ensure concatenated outputs equal original full stream.
Integration: browser example uses fetch streaming to obtain token, persists in localStorage, later resumes and validates no duplicated lines.
Stress: 500 concurrent resume operations to the local dev server to validate locks and rate-limiting penalties.
Performance: measure per-token latency before and after snapshot instrumentation; ensure regression <5%.
Cross-runner: tests in Node 18 CI, Deno (compat shim), and Chrome headless for WebStream behaviors.
decisions: Make snapshot token opaque to SDK consumers to avoid coupling to internal offsets.
Do not implement local cryptographic signing in client; server will issue token and validate on resume.
Expose minimal helper surface; prioritize examples over many overloaded APIs.
Use an adaptive buffering strategy when bridging AsyncIterator -> WebStream to preserve backpressure while minimizing duplication risk.
